messages.content:
Build a post-apocalyptic loot auto-battler. It's fully text-based, mobile-first but responsive enough to work with mouse and keyboard on desktop too. The player scavenges ruined locations for gear, equips it into a backpack, and fights auto-resolved battles where item stats and combos determine the outcome — no manual combat input, the build does the fighting.

For feel, borrow from Scavenge Wars the location-based looting loop: visiting a ruined location carries a real chance of an ambush that costs you items or energy, not just a guaranteed reward. Borrow from Backpack Brawl the equip mechanic: items slot into a limited backpack, and their combined properties (damage type, defense, rarity) roll up into an overall power level — call it "weight class" — that roughly predicts who wins a matchup, the way a heavier loadout usually beats a scrappier one.

Screens: Loot Locations, Backpack/Inventory, Arena, and a light Trader Outpost. Everything is text and UI, no camera or spatial rendering. Items and log entries are colored strictly by rarity tier — common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, and a distinct color reserved for one-of-a-kind items — so the player can read power level at a glance.

The v1 loop: player taps a loot location card (trigger). The game rolls the location event — either an item find or an ambush (action). On a find, the item drops into loose inventory; on a lost ambush, an item or energy is removed (result), logged as a colored text entry with a short flavor line (feedback). The player then drags or taps found items into backpack slots, watching their weight class total update live as they swap gear. From there they enter the Arena and pick an opponent from a pool of saved player builds — async, no live matchmaking, just battling against a snapshot of how someone else's backpack was equipped — with a handful of seeded NPC "veteran" builds mixed in early so the pool isn't empty on day one. The battle auto-resolves with a quick text log of exchanges, and the winner earns currency plus a chance at an item reward roughly matched to the tiers involved. Returning to the game after time away shows a short popup: how many battles happened passively against the player's own build while they were gone, wins, losses, and currency gained. The Trader Outpost is present but light for v1: simple buy and sell of items, plus one or two basic consumables like an energy-restoring recovery juice — no research system, no deep pricing economy yet.

Tone is dry post-apocalyptic scavenger humor — a legendary-tier item can absolutely be a paperclip. A good session looks like: loot a location, find something usable, adjust the backpack, run a couple of arena battles, and walk away with more currency or gear than you started with, watching your weight class creep upward over several sessions. There's no game-over state — losing a fight or an ambush just costs items or currency and the loop continues.

Setting: Plague & rot
Starting feel: Found a stash
Tone: Dry & deadpan

---

**Audio (procedural — zero assets, instant playback)**
- Low sub-bass drone (55 Hz + 82.5 Hz fifth), slow-breathing LFO, filtered noise floor, and occasional distant metallic pings — starts the moment you enter the game
- `playClick()` — tab switches
- `playScavenge()` — noise burst + low thud when you tap a location
- `playItemFound(rarity)` — 1–4 ascending tones scaled to rarity, with a 4-note chime + sparkle for unique paperclips
- `playBattleWin()` / `playBattleLoss()` — punchy sweep up vs descending drone
- `playBuy()` — soft double-tick at the Outpost
- Mute state syncs from save on boot and on any toggle change

**Retention mechanics**

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Daily login bonus** | First open each day awards 15–60 scrip (15 base +5/day, caps at streak 7). A 7-pip streak tracker shows progress. Pops up on the menu screen. |
| **Energy notifications** | On sleep/quit, schedules a local push notification for when energy hits max. Uses `collapseKey: energy-full` so re-scheduling never stacks. |
| **Research notifications** | Whenever items are queued (loot or arena win), schedules a notification for the soonest-completing item. Supersedes itself automatically. |
| **Daily scavenge challenge** | One location highlighted each day (seeded from the date, rotates through all 8 locations). Visiting it awards **+25 scrip** the first time. Badge shows "DAILY +25" in orange; changes to "DONE TODAY" once claimed. |

Add a lore layer built around the Terra's — the game's mutated-mammal creatures, altered by an unspecified infection into distinct variants. This should stay atmospheric and optional, not a new core system layered on top of the existing loop.

There are two ways lore surfaces. First, when a Terra ambushes the player during looting, occasionally attach a short lore snippet to the encounter's text log alongside the normal ambush description — something specific to that creature. Second, loot locations can occasionally drop a standalone lore item into inventory, separate from gear, that reads as a found document rather than something equippable.

Vary the format of these snippets rather than locking to one style, so the world feels lived-in and unreliable. Some read like a survivor's handwritten journal entry. Some read like a clinical research log documenting the infection. Some are fragments of an old radio broadcast, half-corrupted. Some are just short, cryptic one-liners with no clear author. Mix these naturally so two in a row rarely feel the same.

Add a lightweight Bestiary screen, where each Terra variant gets its own entry. An entry starts blank until the player has encountered that variant through an ambush or found a lore item tied to it, at which point it fills in with whatever snippets have been collected for that creature so far. Entries don't need completion tracking, rewards, or mechanical effects yet — just a growing, browsable collection. Tone stays dry and grim to match the wasteland setting, not campy, even when a snippet is darkly funny.

On the title screen should be a Lore button that briefly goes over what this world is, and a tagline of being able to get more lore in game.
